title: Percussion Musical Instruments (Drawing)
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Bring real or improvised instruments: a drum, a kayamba, shakers, a set of tuned bottles. Community names are for a teacher to confirm.

skills.key_step: The child names Kenyan percussion instruments, says each is hit, shaken or scraped, and keeps string and wind instruments out of the group.

floor.question: Is the nyatiti played by plucking or hitting?

steps: Look at how the instrument makes its sound.
Hit, shaken or scraped means percussion.
Plucked is string; blown is wind.
Say the community it comes from.
contexts: a Luhya isukuti dance at a school festival
a kayamba in a coastal song
a church choir with a drum

board.do: Hold up a drum and a nyatiti.

board.say: Is it hit, shaken or plucked?

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a percussion instrument?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: do you hit it, pluck it or blow it? Sort five instruments by that one question.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a percussion instrument?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who makes the sound: the breath, a plucking finger or a hit?

listen_for: It is hit with two sticks
misconceptions.repair: Shake a tin of seeds and listen: the seeds hit the walls and make the sound.

misconceptions.ask: The isukuti drums belong mainly to which people?
misconceptions.repair: Use a map of Kenya and a recording of isukuti to link the sound to the Luhya of western Kenya.

checks.question: Which is a percussion instrument: orutu, isukuti or nzumari?
checks.shows: sorting by how it is played

skills.key_step: The child sorts percussion instruments by whether they can play notes of different pitch (melodic) or not (non-melodic), never by loudness.

floor.prerequisite: Tells long and short sounds apart (Grade 3).
floor.question: Is a clap a long or a short sound?

representations: tuned bottles with different water levels
steps: Ask: can it go higher and lower?
Yes means melodic; no means non-melodic.
contexts: tuned bottles at a school concert

board.do: Tap three bottles with different water.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a melodic instrument?
misconceptions.repair: Play one drum hard and soft: the note does not change. Then play a xylophone bar by bar.

listen_for: Yes, every instrument makes a sound
misconceptions.repair: Shake the kayamba and try to hum a tune with it. Then do the same on tuned bars.
Play a non-melodic shaker in a rhythm: it sounds good but has one sound.

listen_for: melodic, it plays with the song
misconceptions.ask: Is the kayamba melodic or non-melodic?
misconceptions.repair: Shake the kayamba softly and loudly: ask if the note goes up or down. It never does.

checks.question: Is a xylophone melodic or non-melodic?
A drum is very loud. Does that make it melodic?
checks.answer: No, loudness does not decide it

skills.key_step: The child says the skin vibrates to make the sound, the shell makes it fuller, and tightness and size change the pitch.

floor.prerequisite: Knows that sound comes from things that shake.
floor.question: What happens to a ruler that you twang on a desk?
floor.answer: it shakes and makes a sound

representations: a ruler on a desk edge
steps: Hit the skin and feel it shake.
Name the part and its job.
Tighten or loosen: say what happens to the pitch.
contexts: a drummer warming the skin by the fire to tighten it
a big and a small drum in a band

board.do: Point at the skin, shell and stick.

misconceptions.ask: What part of a drum vibrates to make the main sound?
misconceptions.repair: Lay a few grains on the skin and tap it: the grains jump. Touch the shell: it hardly moves.

misconceptions.ask: A drummer tightens the skin. What happens to the sound?
misconceptions.repair: Tap a plastic sheet held loose and then held tight over a bowl.

misconceptions.ask: Which drum gives the lower sound?
misconceptions.repair: Hit a small and a big tin and listen: the big one sounds lower.

listen_for: It makes the sound by itself
misconceptions.ask: What does the drum stick do?
misconceptions.repair: Hit the stick on the floor: only a small tap. Hit it on the drum: a big sound.

checks.question: Which part of the drum shakes to make the sound?
Which gives the lower sound: a big drum or a small drum?

skills.key_step: The child orders the steps of making charcoal sticks (an adult does the fire) and says smudging makes soft light and dark tones.

floor.question: What shape is the top of a drum?

representations: twigs, foil and a tin (shown, not lit)
a charcoal drawing of a drum
a value strip from light to dark
steps: Seal them in foil or a tin.
An adult burns them with little air; let them cool.
Draw, then smudge for soft tones.
contexts: an art lesson drawing a drum
a teacher preparing charcoal before class

board.do: Write the four steps in mixed order.

listen_for: In an open fire until they turn to ash
misconceptions.ask: How are the twigs burned to make charcoal sticks?
misconceptions.repair: Show wood char in a tin with a tight lid: it stays black and in shape because little air gets in.

misconceptions.ask: What must happen before the charcoal is used?
misconceptions.repair: Say: hot charcoal burns the skin and stays hot inside for a long time.

misconceptions.ask: What does smudging do in a charcoal drawing?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a dark patch and rub it with a finger: it spreads into a soft shade.

misconceptions.ask: How do you make a darker area with charcoal?
misconceptions.repair: Make three strokes with light, medium and hard pressure and compare.

checks.question: Why are the twigs sealed before burning?
checks.answer: so they get little air and turn to charcoal, not ash

checks.question: What does smudging do to a charcoal drawing?
checks.answer: it spreads the charcoal into soft light and dark tones
